reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates longer, sustained runs at an easy pace, which is crucial for building the aerobic base necessary for trail running speed. Plan B’s focus on solely easy runs, while beneficial for recovery, lacks the volume and specific endurance work needed to improve speed. Plan A’s inclusion of cross-training also adds a valuable element for maintaining fitness without the impact of trail running. While Plan B prioritizes recovery, Plan A’s structure is more directly geared towards the athlete’s goal of increasing speed.
